description: A species-by-species guide to watching wildlife in India: the best places to look for tigers, Asiatic lions, leopards, snow leopards, one-horned rhinos, elephants, the Indian wild ass, red pandas, hoolock gibbons, lion-tailed macaques, Nilgiri tahr, gharials, Irrawaddy dolphins, sangai and hangul deer and more, with seasons and links to detailed guides.
dek: From tigers to red pandas, most of India's signature animals live in a few well-known places. Here is where to look for each one.

intro: India's wildlife is spread across very different landscapes: the Himalaya, the terai grasslands, central Indian forests, the Western Ghats, the deserts of the west, the mangroves of the east and the hills of the north-east. Each animal has a few places where it is most often seen by visitors.
This guide lists those places species by species. Population figures come from the most recent official estimates, and seasons are typical ones. Every park sets its own dates, so check before you go.
quickAnswer: Tigers are most often seen in central Indian reserves and in Ranthambore and Corbett; Asiatic lions only in Gir; one-horned rhinos in Kaziranga and Pobitora; leopards at Jawai, Jhalana and Kabini; snow leopards in Hemis in winter. Red pandas live in Singalila and Neora Valley, hoolock gibbons in Assam's Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary, and gharials in the Chambal. Most parks are open from October to June.
takeaways: Most signature animals are seen most reliably in a handful of places.
Gir is the only wild home of Asiatic lions; the Little Rann of the Indian wild ass.
India has an estimated 3,682 tigers (2022) and 718 snow leopards (2024 assessment).
North-east India holds red pandas, gibbons and golden langurs.
Plan around seasons: winter for snow leopards and birds, summer for tigers at waterholes.

items.name: Tigers
body: India had an estimated 3,682 tigers in the 2022 assessment, the largest share of the world's wild tigers, led by Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Uttarakhand.

items.name: Leopards
body: Leopards are widespread, but open rocky country such as Jawai and Jhalana gives some of the best views.

items.name: Snow leopards
body: Treks with trackers in the Ladakh winter give a real chance of a sighting, though never a certainty.

sections.heading: Rhinos, elephants and other large mammals

items.name: One-horned rhino
body: Kaziranga holds most of India's rhinos (2,613 in the 2022 count), with more at Pobitora, Orang and Manas in Assam and Jaldapara in West Bengal.

image.alt: A one-horned rhinoceros grazing in tall grass in Jaldapara National Park
image.caption: A rhino in Jaldapara, West Bengal

items.name: Asian elephant
body: Corbett, Kabini, Periyar, Kaziranga and the Dooars have large herds; Kabini's backwaters draw them in summer.

items.name: Indian wild ass
body: Found only in and around the Little Rann of Kutch.

items.name: Gaur, barasingha and blackbuck
body: Gaur in Kanha, Tadoba and the Western Ghats; hard-ground barasingha in Kanha; blackbuck at Velavadar (Gujarat) and Tal Chhapar (Rajasthan).

image.alt: An Indian gaur standing in forest in Trishna Wildlife Sanctuary, Tripura
image.caption: A gaur in Tripura

sections.heading: The north-east and the Himalaya
list: Red panda: Singalila National Park and Neora Valley National Park in West Bengal, and forests in Sikkim and Arunachal.
Hoolock gibbon: Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary near Jorhat, Assam.
Golden langur: Manas National Park and nearby forests in western Assam.
Sangai (brow-antlered deer): Keibul Lamjao National Park, Manipur.
Hangul (Kashmir stag): Dachigam National Park near Srinagar.

sections.heading: The Western Ghats
list: Lion-tailed macaque: the rainforest around Valparai in the Anamalai hills, Tamil Nadu.
Nilgiri tahr: Eravikulam National Park near Munnar.
Grizzled giant squirrel: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary, Kerala.
Sloth bear: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary near Hampi, as well as Satpura and Tadoba.

sections.heading: Rivers and coasts
list: Gharial and Gangetic dolphin: the National Chambal Sanctuary, on the Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh border.
Irrawaddy dolphin: Chilika lake, Odisha, especially near Satapada.
Saltwater crocodile: Bhitarkanika National Park, Odisha, and the Sundarbans.
Olive ridley turtles: mass nesting beaches in Odisha, such as Gahirmatha and Rushikulya, in the late winter months.
after: Nesting and dolphin seasons vary; check with local forest offices.

sections.heading: Combining species on one trip
list: Central India: tigers, leopards, gaur, sloth bears and dhole across Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench and Satpura.
Assam: rhinos, elephants, wild buffalo, gibbons and golden langurs across Kaziranga, Hollongapar and Manas.
Gujarat: lions in Gir, wild ass in the Little Rann and blackbuck at Velavadar.
Karnataka and Kerala: elephants, leopards, tigers and Nilgiri tahr across Kabini, Bandipur and Munnar.

safety: Sightings are never guaranteed; wild animals move freely and every drive is different.
Follow park rules on vehicles, walking and distance.
Never feed or approach wild animals.
Use licensed guides in every protected area.

faqs.q: Where can I see the most wildlife in India?
faqs.a: Kaziranga for variety in one park; central India's tiger reserves for big cats; Kabini for elephants and leopards.

faqs.q: Where can I see red pandas in India?
faqs.a: In Singalila and Neora Valley national parks in West Bengal, and in forests in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

faqs.q: How many tigers are there in India?
faqs.a: The 2022 assessment estimated 3,682 tigers. A new count began in 2026.

faqs.q: How many snow leopards are there in India?
faqs.a: The 2024 national assessment estimated 718, most of them in Ladakh.

faqs.q: Where can I see dolphins in India?
faqs.a: Irrawaddy dolphins at Chilika lake and Gangetic dolphins in the Chambal and parts of the Ganga.
